scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Vattakkali is an ancestral tradition of the Vattuvar community, a group indigenous to the state of Kerala.
Historically, it has been preserved as a part of the Kanyarkali (or Kanniyar Kali) tradition, which is a fast-moving dance-drama performed in the temples of the Palakkad district.
The dance serves as a communal expression of identity and devotion, particularly during the post-harvest season of Onam.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Vattakkali is performed during the Onam festival season and as a vital component of the Kanyarkali Mahotsavam.
It carries ritual significance, particularly when performed in temples, where it may be accompanied by offerings of flowers.
The dance represents communal harmony and the celebration of the harvest, serving as a ritualistic folk expression for the Vattuvar people.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a circular formation where participants move in 'vigorous ring patterns.' The core of the technique consists of twelve different types of steps, which are executed with increasing speed.
Dancers use rhythmic hand clapping to maintain the beat while their feet perform intricate patterns.
Watch for Twelve Chuvadu, Whirling Ring.

Formation: A tight circular ring that moves vigorously as a unit

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music for Vattakkali is primarily vocal, consisting of songs sung by the group of dancers themselves.
The rhythmic accompaniment is generated internally by the performers through hand clapping and the use of 'tinkling anklets and bells' worn on the feet.
Listen for the Anklets, Bells, Hand claps.
The pulse is Typically 4/4 or 8-beat cycles common in Kerala folk music at about 85 beats a minute.
The sound is dominated by the collective voices of the men singing in unison, punctuated by the sharp, metallic 'tinkling' of bells and the percussive 'thud' of rhythmic stamping on the ground.

Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Steady stamping and clapping that doubles in speed during the climax

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The dance is traditionally performed in the temples of Palakkad during the Kanyarkali Mahotsavam.
Dancers typically wear traditional Kerala attire, which usually consists of a mundu (waist cloth).
The most significant functional element of the costume is the set of bells or anklets.
